title: Hof operation lock (v2, kind-generic)
description: /var/lib/hof/state/lock.json - exclusive ownership of an in-progress or interrupted operation against this host. Identical to operation-lock-v1 except for the added operationKind field (ADR 0006): apply, backup, and restore now all share one physical execution mutex, refusing each other in every direction, not just same-kind contention. A pre-existing lock.json written before this ADR has no operationKind field at all and does not validate against this schema - an executor reading it must treat that absence as an implicit "apply" (operation-lock-v1 is still valid, still readable, never deleted). Deliberately has no TTL/expiry field - the lock must survive the invoking process dying (an operator's laptop sleeping, a network drop), so it is only ever removed by a successful commit or reclaimed by --resume for the SAME operationId, never by simply waiting it out.

operationKind.description: Which of the three operation state machines this lock belongs to - the whole reason this schema exists rather than reusing operation-lock-v1 unchanged. A backup or restore in progress refuses a concurrent apply against the same target, and vice versa, exactly as an apply already refuses a concurrent apply.

operationId.description: This operation's own unique identifier - ties the lock to its operation journal (same field name) and to every operation-event-v1 record it emits.

approvedPlanId.description: The approved plan's own planId - a plan-v2, backup-plan-v1, or restore-plan-v1 planId depending on operationKind (all three use the same sha256-of-inputs shape).

acquiredBy.description: Informational only, for a human debugging a stuck lock - never used for an actual security decision (the lock's own operationId is the only thing that authorizes a resume).

targetBinding.description: The exact target this operation was approved against - see plan-v2.schema.json's own `target` for the full description of each field. Duplicated here (not $ref'd across files - no schema in this repo cross-references another by $id) so this schema stays independently valid on its own.

hostKeySha256.description: The exact accepted SSH host-key fingerprint from the same connection the bound plan was computed against - null only in --target-mode local. A host-key change invalidates every plan bound to the old one.
